cmdb_ci.name: Emergency Break-Glass Administrator
cmdb_ci.short_description: Registered emergency break-glass administrator account. Standing super-administrator held under seal for production emergencies; every use is ticket-gated and audited. This account is a required control and must remain available.

incident.description:
SOC alerting flagged a sign-in and administrative activity from the registered break-glass emergency administrator account overnight (16 Jul), with no approved break-glass authorisation on file for that window. Break-glass use is strictly ticket-gated, so this session is treated as unauthorised.

Reconstruct everything this account did during the session from the identity provider's system log, and unwind the session so the environment is returned to its pre-session state. Secure the break-glass account itself and keep it available as an emergency control. Other, authorised administrative activity from the same night must be left intact. Close this incident when the environment has been restored.
incident.short_description: Out-of-policy use of the break-glass emergency administrator account

incident.close_notes: Reconstructed the break-glass session from the Okta System Log by filtering on the actor across the session window, and reversed exactly what that session had done and nothing else. Crucially, the session did not only act under the break-glass account itself: it had created a service account and used it, so we followed the create-chain in the log - revoking the admin roles the session granted directly (a group review alone would have missed those), removing the users it added to privileged groups, deactivating every service account the session created AND unwinding the changes those created accounts had in turn made (including a further account one of them had created), un-enrolling the MFA factors it planted on existing administrators for re-entry, and removing the SSO application assignments it added. We then rotated the break-glass credential and revoked its sessions, but kept the account itself - it is a required emergency control. A couple of legitimate changes made by other administrators the same night (each with an approved change on file) were verified and left untouched. Environment confirmed back to its pre-session state.
incident.description: Earlier unauthorised use of the emergency break-glass administrator account; reconstructed and unwound the session.
incident.short_description: Break-glass administrator account misuse - session remediation
